status_legend.BY_DESIGN: Intentional architecture constraint rather than an unresolved defect.

p0.name: failed-task-resubmission
p0.implementation: Duplicate detection blocks open, running, completed and duplicate predecessors, but failed/not_planned history does not poison a new Issue fingerprint.
p0.production_acceptance: Governance Issue 84 repeated failed Issue 79, received new task_id gov-84-expert and a new child Issue rather than CONTROL_DUPLICATE.

p0.name: comment-pagination
p0.implementation: Governance child monitoring, retry accounting and status ownership checks scan up to ten pages of 100 comments.
p0.production_acceptance: No destructive 1000-comment live fixture was executed; deterministic pagination coverage is the current evidence boundary.

p0.name: task-id-binding
p0.implementation: Monitoring accepts only the governance-generated task_id. Missing or mismatched Task ID terminals remain provisional and do not end polling.
p0.production_acceptance: Governance Issue 84 stayed open after an unbound expert rejection and completed only after the task-bound gov-84-expert rejection arrived.

p0.name: artifact-contract
p0.implementation: Compute/API success requires Artifact ID, 64-hex digest and matching Artifact URL. Expert success additionally requires primary and final-attestation Artifact identities.
p0.production_acceptance: Compute Issues 78 and 88 and intelligence Issue 90 were accepted only with exact task-bound Artifact identities.

p0.name: late-terminal-reconciliation
p0.implementation: A serialized worker reconciles only owner-authored canonical [control] timeout or monitor-error records, derives task_id from the governance Issue number, enforces the route-fixed child repository and applies absorbing Artifact-backed success precedence.
p0.production_acceptance: Governance Issue 90 changed from CONTROL_TIMEOUT to CONTROL_RECONCILED_LATE_SUCCESS with state_reason completed, child API_COMPLETED, Artifact ID 8906242150 and digest 456940a9deb4b492adb0394c8976d2f43045ea5bf177195b69b91cfb344e6a59. A later already-accepted API_REJECTED did not revoke the completed success.

p0.name: lost-trigger-recovery
p0.implementation: When no trusted child bot activity is observed, governance performs at most one marker-bound recovery: close/reopen for compute/API or one exact expert command repost.
p0.production_acceptance: Governance Issue 88 reused compute Issue 109, wrote exactly one Recovery attempt 1/1 marker, reopened the child, obtained COMPUTE_COMPLETED with Artifact ID 8906239829 and reconciled to CONTROL_RECONCILED_LATE_SUCCESS with state_reason completed.

p0.name: gpts-trusted-comment-read
p0.implementation: Repository OpenAPI exposes one additional read-only governance Issue comments operation. No child-repository or mutation operation is exposed.
p0.operational_boundary: A custom GPT does not automatically import a changed repository OpenAPI file. The Action schema must be updated in the GPT configuration before live acceptance of the comments operation.
p0.production_acceptance: Pending manual custom-GPT schema import; repository permission and interface contracts pass.

p0.name: json-complexity-and-secret-variants
p0.implementation: The gateway bounds body size, JSON depth, node count, key length and string length, and rejects camelCase authorization/secret variants plus executable field names.
p0.production_acceptance: Governance Issue 80 rejected clientSecret and pythonCode with zero child dispatch and zero model/API/compute calls.

p1.name: github-rate-limit-and-network-backoff
p1.implementation: The resilient transport retries HTTP 429, rate-limit 403, HTTP 502/503/504 and short network failures with bounded attempts and backoff, while ordinary 403/4xx fail immediately.
p1.boundary: GitHub platform-wide outages remain operational dependencies.

p1.name: bounded-next-worker-wake
p1.implementation: The next FIFO worker is awakened at 0, 5 and 15 seconds. Exhaustion publishes CONTROL_QUEUE_WAKE_DEGRADED and preserves the open Issue queue for the 15-minute scheduled worker.

p1.name: daily-token-and-repository-health
p1.implementation: A daily zero-business-call health workflow validates four repository identities, positive Issue access and negative Contents/Actions-Secrets permissions, maintaining one health Issue only on failure.
p1.boundary: Exact hidden fine-grained PAT checkboxes cannot be read back through repository APIs; runtime positive and negative permission behavior is the enforceable evidence.

p1.name: user-facing-status-dictionary
p1.implementation: A machine-readable dictionary defines terminality, user meaning and next action for control, timeout, reconciliation, queue-degradation and platform-unavailable states.

p1.name: issue-and-artifact-retention-policy
p1.implementation: Closed Issues remain as durable task indexes, Artifacts use explicit retention and long-term archival must preserve task_id, run, commit, Artifact ID and digest.
p1.boundary: GitHub Artifact retention is not indefinite; external long-term archival is a separate future operation.

operational_boundaries: GitHub platform-wide outages cannot be bypassed without violating the evidence architecture.
Closing an Issue does not cancel an already-running child workflow because the control token intentionally has no Actions write permission.
Exact hidden fine-grained PAT settings for the custom GPT cannot be read back through repository APIs.
The updated OpenAPI file must be imported into the custom GPT before the read-only comments operation is available there.
P0-02 has deterministic pagination evidence but no destructive 1000-comment live fixture.
Artifact retention is finite unless a separate governed archive is configured.
